Extremely skilled boxer. There are some impressive videos of him in action, just go through YouTube and watch some highlight reels of his fights. The gif of him "dodging 21 punches in 10 seconds" isn't too much of an exaggeration.

Quick summary: He's a heavy hitter who had a very effective dodge. This is important because many heavyweight matches are endurance fights - it takes a lot of energy to throw that many punches. If he can bob and weave and take less hits than the other guy, he'll still be fresh while the opponent is tired from punching air. This was also a paradigm shift in boxing, as many heavyweights at that time were so large they focused on durability instead of dodging.

Even after the draft-dodging events banned him from boxing for ~4 years, he was still a powerhouse. He couldn't bob and weave like before, but his guard was so strong he could still use his original strategy of "tire out the enemy, when they get sloppy hit em hard" to great effect. Because this "rope a dope" strategy involved taking a lot of hits, he ended up with some serious brain damage from his boxing career and later on in life it was pretty sad to see him so punch-drunk. He was always pretty good to his fans and seemed like a nice, caring guy.
